thread:
Anna: Drafting a PRD checklist for generation API edge cases. Need a concise enumeration to validate before launch — streaming, truncation, retries, token accounting, and resume semantics.
Chris: +1. Please include model-fallback behavior and resume-token contract.
Jamal: Customer reported streaming cut mid-JSON and their parser crashed. Acceptance idea: either guarantee JSON atomicity or surface a resume_token + clear final flag.
Maya: Proposed acceptance: every streaming session includes metadata frames: {stream_id, resume_token?, final:true|false}. If final=false clients can attempt resume.
Anna: Quick edge list I sketched:
  1) Streaming truncates mid-token or mid-UTF8 char.
  2) Retry yields duplicated prefix (idempotency issue).
  3) Token limit reached mid-stream (hard vs soft limit).
  4) Model stalls with no error (early stop).
  5) Rollout switches model mid-request.
  6) Client reconnect after intermittent network loss.
  7) Resume across quantized/variant model fallback.
CI Bot: build/stream-resume-tests: failing on linux-x86 in integration job 427.
Chris: For retries we should require a client-supplied request_id. If server receives same request_id, server must either return the same completed output or return a resume_token that deterministically resumes from where the client left off. Add acceptance test asserting strict idempotency.
Jamal: Also add UTF-8/truncation rule: truncation must not split a multi-byte codepoint in the last transmitted chunk. If unavoidable, include a byte-trim marker and a resume_token pointing to safe token boundary.
Maya: Truncation acceptance criteria proposal: when truncation happens because of token_limit, response must include: truncated=true, truncation_reason:"token_limit", last_token_index, and resume_token if resumable. For embeddings endpoints we must also return partial_embedding with a flag.
Anna: Scope note: mark streaming JSON-atomicity P1 for Hosted API; P2 for Dedicated and Private for now. Rationale: many customers rely on sync parsers.
Chris: Network interruption behavior: client reconnect should present resume_token + last_received_token_index. Server supports resumability for up to 5 minutes after initial session and only within same model+version. Add test harness for reconnect within that window.
Jamal: Edge-case: model_rollout switch mid-request — server should prefer failing fast with 503 + {retryable:true} rather than silently swapping model and producing inconsistent output. Document expected behavior for rollouts.
Maya: Tests to add: fuzz disconnects during streaming, long prefix scenarios (prefix > 80% of context), and token_overflow stress. Also update SDKs with examples for resume_token use:
```
// Node example (pseudocode)
const res = await client.stream({prompt, request_id: 'r-123'});
res.on('data', chunk => save(chunk.resume_token));
// on reconnect: client.resume({resume_token: lastToken, request_id: 'r-123'});
```
Anna: Ops acceptance: observability must record per-stream metrics: bytes_sent, tokens_emitted, resume_count, truncation_count, resume_latency. These metrics are required for launch.
Chris: For the PRD acceptance suite I'll draft: (a) deterministic-retry test, (b) resume-in-5min test, (c) truncation-metadata test, (d) model-rollout-abort test.
Jamal: Note to docs: explain difference between "truncated=true" and "final=false" so integrators don't conflate them.
Maya: I'll add SDK usage examples and a short migration note for customers parsing streamed JSON.
Anna: OK I'll incorporate these items into the PRD checklist and ping @Chris/@Maya for the acceptance artifacts. Thanks — I'll circulate the draft later today.
